title: Chest Pain

correct_orders.rationale: Good diagnostic step to confirm tension pneumothorax. However, chest tube must follow to prevent recurrence.

rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: It is always important to see how the patient looks in general to assess how sick the patient is.
rationale.Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs: Evaluate chest/lungs in a patient with respiratory distress.
rationale.Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular: Cardiovascular evaluation provides key information in respiratory distress. Only focused exam needed in emergency.
rationale.Physical Exam: Extremities / Spine: Symptoms could result from PE — evaluate extremities for signs of DVT.
rationale.Pulse oximetry: Patient in respiratory distress — check pulse oximetry.
rationale.Electrocardiography, 12 lead: Initial EKG to rule out myocardial infarction.
rationale.Cardiac troponin I, serum: Troponins should be evaluated — patient has chest pain, MI must be ruled out.
rationale.Thoracentesis: Good diagnostic step to confirm tension pneumothorax. However, chest tube must follow to prevent recurrence.
rationale.Tube thoracostomy / Needle thoracostomy: Chest tube should be placed after needle thoracostomy and placed to suction.
rationale.Chest X-ray (post-procedure): X-ray verifies chest tube placement AFTER insertion. Do NOT diagnose by X-ray — tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis. Imaging before tube placement loses points.
rationale.Chest X-ray (before intervention): Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis. Imaging before decompression causes dangerous delay.
rationale.CT chest with contrast: CT causes unacceptable delay in a life-threatening emergency.
rationale.Echocardiogram: Too time-consuming. Immediate decompression is the priority.
rationale.D-dimer, serum: While PE is on the differential, exam findings point to tension pneumothorax. Decompress first.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents to the emergency department with acute onset chest pain and severe respiratory distress. The patient appears diaphoretic, tachypneic, and in extremis. Symptoms began suddenly with rapid progression. Exam reveals unilateral absence of breath sounds, tracheal deviation, and hyperresonance on percussion. Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis made at the bedside — immediate intervention is critical and must not be delayed for imaging.

physical_exam: Tachycardic; assess for muffled heart sounds and JVD.
Unilateral absence of breath sounds. Tracheal deviation. Hyperresonance on affected side.
